holidays.name: World Freedom Day
holidays.description: A day celebrating the fall of the Berlin Wall in 1989 and the triumph of liberty over oppression. Celebrated with events, speeches, and reflections on the value of freedom around the world.
holidays.origin: Established by U.S. President George W. Bush in 2001 and proclaimed annually to mark the anniversary of the Berlin Wall opening on November 9, 1989.
holidays.funFact: The Berlin Wall's fall was partly an accident: East German spokesman Günter Schabowski mistakenly announced that new travel rules took effect 'immediately, without delay,' sending crowds rushing to the border.

holidays.name: Chaos Never Dies Day
holidays.description: A tongue-in-cheek day for embracing the unpredictable madness of life. Celebrants toss out their schedules, let things get messy, and accept that disorder is just part of the universe.
holidays.origin: An unofficial, internet-era observance listed in quirky holiday calendars, created to celebrate the beauty of disorder and the fact that no plan survives contact with reality.
holidays.funFact: Entropy, the scientific measure of disorder, always increases in a closed system, so technically the universe is on Team Chaos.

holidays.name: Go to an Art Museum Day
holidays.description: A day for wandering through galleries, squinting thoughtfully at abstract paintings, and pretending you understand what the artist meant by a single red chair in an empty room.
holidays.origin: A cultural observance promoted by museum enthusiasts and arts groups to encourage people to visit their local galleries and support the arts.
holidays.funFact: The Louvre in Paris is the most visited art museum in the world, and it would take roughly 100 days to look at every piece for just 30 seconds each.

holidays.name: Carl Sagan Day
holidays.description: A celebration of the beloved astronomer and science communicator, who inspired millions to look up at the cosmos. Fans gaze at the stars, quote 'billions and billions,' and ponder our pale blue dot.
holidays.origin: Observed on Carl Sagan's birthday, November 9, 1934. Science fans and educators mark the day to promote scientific curiosity and wonder.
holidays.funFact: Sagan helped design the Golden Records aboard the Voyager spacecraft, which carry greetings in 55 languages, music, and sounds of Earth into interstellar space.

holidays.name: Cliche Day
holidays.description: A day to embrace every overused phrase in the book. Avoiding clichés like the plague is not an option today, as it is what it is at the end of the day.
holidays.origin: An unofficial humorous observance, popular on quirky holiday calendars, inviting people to play with tired idioms and sayings.
holidays.funFact: The word 'cliché' comes from a French printing term for a stereotype printing plate, which produced the same impression over and over again.
